acceptance: Every PySpark SF1 cell has a best-time pair, or is recorded as not runnable with the exact refusal or failure.
SF10 cells are run on a host that can hold them, or recorded as not run with the host's memory and the guard's stated requirement.
Each gate has a recorded outcome (kept, changed with the PR, or escalated), with the tables in this item.
The two timing worktrees are removed when the work ends.
context: Depends on the memory-guard fix so that a refusal states the real threshold; that fix does not lower the requirement, so a quiet host is still needed for PySpark at SF1 (about 3.6 GiB free for a 3.0 GiB estimate).
description:
Problem. Three merged changes altered how DataFrame queries test for more than one distinct value: TPC-DS Q16/Q94/Q95 min/max (PR #4169), Polars `n_unique()` skipping NULL (PR #4169), and Q21 filtering its per-order aggregates before joining (PR #4196). They were timed at SF1 on Polars 1.44.2 and DataFusion 54.0.0 only (results in `df-distinct-timing-confirmation`). They are unmeasured on PySpark at any scale and on every engine at SF10, because BenchBox's memory guard refused those runs on the 16 GiB development host: PySpark at SF1 with messages such as `~3.0 GB required, but only 2.7 GB available`, and SF10 with an estimate of 18-20 GiB. PySpark took the same code change as the other engines, so a regression there would be in published PySpark numbers unnoticed.

Method. Compare commit 0eeec0d5bd194ad0b811911ea73004586ed51469 (before PR #4169) with current `develop` in two checkouts made by `make worktree-create`. Alternate checkouts; one warm-up then at least five timed runs a side per round, five rounds; compare best times. Check the 1-minute load average only before each round (the benchmark's own load must not discard a round). Record engine versions and the load seen.

Cells: PySpark at SF1 for TPC-DS Q16, Q94, Q95; TPC-H Q21; Data Vault Q21; TPC-Havoc Q21 variants 1 and 4-10. All three engines at SF10 for the same queries, where the host can hold the data.

Decision gates, ratio changed/base on best times: above 1.10 on any cell means the pattern is changed or reverted on every platform (no platform-name branch), keeping the NULL fixes; if no form is within 1.10 on all engines, stop and ask the owner. A change that is neither faster nor slower stays.

Guardrails: timing only through `make heavy-run` after `make heavy-status`; never force admission, skip the test lock, or disable the watchdog without the owner's approval in that task; `--ignore-memory-warnings` likewise needs the owner's approval. Harness scripts are throwaway and not committed; the earlier ones are in ~/Developer/benchmark_runs/df-distinct-remediation/ (timing.py, matrix.py) and point at worktrees that no longer exist. Do not edit SQL text, reference answers, or fixtures.
